en: 1. The Question of the Donkey’s Limb “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one limb of the donkey should be adopted,’ which is that one limb that should be adopted?

“Just as, Great King, the creature called a donkey lies anywhere—at a heap of refuse, at a crossroads, at a junction, at the village gate, or on a pile of chaff—it does not spend much time lying down;”
In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga, a yogāvacara, should spread out a piece of hide anywhere— whether on a bed of grass, a bed of leaves, a wooden frame,
or even on the bare ground— and lie down wherever he may be;
he should not be one who indulges excessively in lying down.
This, Great King, is one quality of the donkey that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was said by the Blessed One, the God above Gods: “Bhikkhus, my disciples now dwell with the skeleton as their support, heedful, ardent, and resolute in striving.
This, Great King, was also said by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:
the knees do not get wet by the rain;
it is sufficient for dwelling in comfort.
The first question, on the breaking of the camel’s neck.
